chapter_summary: Proverbs 14 is a collection of sharp contrasts between the wise and the foolish, the righteous and the wicked. It covers the home, the heart, the tongue, the poor, the king, and the nation — showing that wisdom and folly touch every part of life. A central warning runs through the chapter: things that look right can lead to death, and laughter can hide a grieving heart. The fear of the LORD appears as both a fountain of life and a strong confidence. At every turn, God is concerned not only with what we do but with the direction our heart is truly heading.
main_lesson: Wise choices build up everything around you. Foolish choices tear things down. God sees your heart, and He wants you to walk in His wisdom.

memory_verse.kjv: In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.
memory_verse.little_bible: When you respect and honour God, you have strong confidence. God becomes a safe place for you and your family.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 14 is one of the richest chapters in the book for family discipleship, because it moves through so many domains of ordinary life. The chapter opens with a woman who builds her house and one who tears it down with her own hands — a vivid picture of how daily choices either construct or destroy what matters most. Help your children see that wisdom is not passive; it builds. Foolishness destroys — often without realising it.

The chapter contains one of Scripture's most important warnings: 'There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death' (v. 12). Children need to know early that feelings of rightness are not the same as actual rightness. Our hearts can deceive us. This is why God's Word — not our feelings — is the anchor for our choices.

Verses 26–27 give the theological heart of the chapter: fear of the LORD is a strong confidence and a fountain of life. This is not terror — it is reverential awe and trust. Help your children understand that honouring God is not a burden; it is the source of safety, life, and real confidence. It keeps them from the snares of death.

The chapter also has much to say about the poor (vv. 20–21, 31). God notices how we treat those with less. Despising a poor neighbour is sin; showing mercy is happiness. Oppressing the poor is an insult to God who made them. These are strong statements — do not soften them. Pray with your children that God would give them hearts of genuine compassion.
application_for_children: This week, think before each choice: 'Is this wise or foolish? Will this build up or tear down?' Ask God to help you walk in the fear of the LORD — the safe and living path.

verses.kjv: Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.
verses.little_bible: A wise woman builds her home with her choices. A foolish woman tears her own home down.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise choices build your home. Foolish choices break it.
verses.meaning: The contrast is stark: wisdom actively builds, while folly actively destroys — often without intending to. The image of 'her own hands' underlines that foolishness is self-inflicted destruction. Every daily choice either constructs or tears apart what God has entrusted to us.
verses.prayer: God, help me build, not tear down.
verses.discussion_question: What is one choice that builds up your home?
verses.family_discussion: In what daily ways — attitude, words, habits — do we as a family build our home up or tear it down without realising it?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today that builds up your home — help without being asked, speak kindly, or tidy a shared space.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two women: one carefully placing stones to build a bright warm house, one pulling bricks away from a crumbling home, gentle watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the LORD: but he that is perverse in his ways despiseth him.
verses.little_bible: Living honestly shows that you respect and honour God. Choosing wrong paths shows that you have pushed God aside.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Living right shows you honour God.
verses.meaning: The way we live reveals whether we truly fear the LORD or not. Upright living is not merely moral behaviour — it is the visible expression of honouring God. A perverse way of life is ultimately a rejection of God, whatever one may claim with the mouth.
verses.prayer: God, let my life show I honour You.
verses.discussion_question: How does the way you live show what you really believe?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that faith and obedience are connected — that the way we live tells the real story of what we believe about God?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one part of your daily life. Does it honour God? If not, ask Him to help you change it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child walking a straight glowing path toward a bright light, another figure walking a crooked path in shadow, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: In the mouth of the foolish is a rod of pride: but the lips of the wise shall preserve them.
verses.little_bible: A foolish person's proud words hurt others — like hitting with a stick. But wise words protect and keep you safe.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Proud words hurt. Wise words protect.
verses.meaning: The fool's words are a weapon of pride — striking others and ultimately bringing punishment back on the speaker. Wise speech, by contrast, is a form of protection. Our words have consequences far beyond the moment we speak them.
verses.prayer: God, give me wise and kind words.
verses.discussion_question: How can words hurt like a stick?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand the real power of their words — not just to wound others, but to protect themselves and build trust?
verses.do_it_today: Before you speak today, ask: 'Will these words help or hurt?' Choose helpful words all day.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child's mouth with golden light coming out as gentle words, another with sharp dark lines as proud words, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean: but much increase is by the strength of the ox.
verses.little_bible: No oxen means the barn stays clean. But oxen do the hard work that grows the harvest.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Hard work means some mess. But it brings good results.
verses.meaning: Productivity is messy. The clean crib with no oxen is the picture of ease without fruit. Real increase comes from accepting the effort — and the mess — that comes with diligent work. A risk-free life is often an unfruitful one.
verses.prayer: God, help me do the hard and good work.
verses.discussion_question: Why is something messy sometimes a sign of good work?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children embrace the reality that meaningful work often involves difficulty and mess — and that fruitfulness requires effort, not comfort?
verses.do_it_today: Do a task that is a little hard or messy today. See the good result it brings at the end.
verses.illustration_prompt: A busy barn with an ox working, straw scattered, a full grain basket in the corner, warm golden light, watercolour farming scene

verses.kjv: A faithful witness will not lie: but a false witness will utter lies.
verses.little_bible: A trustworthy person always tells the truth. A dishonest person keeps saying false things.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A faithful witness tells the truth.
verses.meaning: This is about character revealed in testimony. The faithful witness does not lie because truthfulness is who they are — not just what they choose in easy moments. The false witness, by contrast, makes lying a pattern. What we do regularly forms who we become.
verses.prayer: God, make me a person who never lies.
verses.discussion_question: What makes someone a trustworthy witness?
verses.family_discussion: How do we build a family culture where truth-telling is honoured and safe — so children are not afraid to tell the truth even when it costs them?
verses.do_it_today: Tell someone a true thing today even when it would have been easier to stay quiet or bend the truth.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing calmly before others, speaking with a bright light around their words, a clear and honest expression, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not: but knowledge is easy unto him that understandeth.
verses.little_bible: A mocker looks for wisdom but never finds it. The person who is open to learn finds it easily.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Mockers cannot find wisdom. Humble people find it easily.
verses.meaning: The scorner's problem is not lack of intelligence but attitude. A heart that mocks cannot receive wisdom because wisdom requires humility. The person who truly wants to understand finds knowledge accessible — because their heart is open to receive it.
verses.prayer: God, keep my heart humble and open to You.
verses.discussion_question: Why can a proud mocker never find true wisdom?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate genuine teachability in our children — a posture that is open to correction and ready to learn, rather than defensive or dismissive?
verses.do_it_today: Ask someone wiser than you to teach you something today. Receive their teaching without arguing.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with arms open in a learning posture, light and knowledge flowing toward them; beside them a figure with arms crossed and eyes closed, turning away from the same light, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not in him the lips of knowledge.
verses.little_bible: Walk away from a foolish person. If they speak no wisdom, do not stay close to them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Stay away from foolish people and their foolish words.
verses.meaning: Wisdom sometimes means choosing who you spend time with. If someone consistently speaks without knowledge, their company will do harm. This is not unkind — it is a necessary protection of your own mind and character.
verses.prayer: God, help me choose wise friends and companions.
verses.discussion_question: Why does it matter who you spend your time with?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children navigate friendships wisely — knowing when to be a godly influence and when a relationship is doing them harm?
verses.do_it_today: Think about your friendships. Who makes you wiser? Spend more time with them today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child walking calmly away from a group speaking foolishly, heading toward a wiser and brighter path, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way: but the folly of fools is deceit.
verses.little_bible: Wise people think carefully about the path they are on. Foolish people deceive themselves and others.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise people think about where they are going.
verses.meaning: Prudence — careful, thoughtful wisdom — looks honestly at one's own path and direction. Folly, by contrast, operates in deceit: deceiving others and, most dangerously, deceiving oneself. Honest self-examination is a mark of real wisdom.
verses.prayer: God, help me see my path clearly.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to think carefully about the path you are on?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop honest self-reflection — the ability to examine where their choices are actually leading them, not just where they feel like they are going?
verses.do_it_today: Stop today and think: where are my habits and choices taking me? Are you happy with that direction?
verses.illustration_prompt: A thoughtful child looking ahead down a long path, hand on chin in reflection, clear and bright road ahead, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Fools make a mock at sin: but among the righteous there is favour.
verses.little_bible: Foolish people laugh at doing wrong. They think sin is no big deal. But God shows favour to those who do right.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not laugh at sin. Do what is right.
verses.meaning: Treating sin as something to joke about is deeply foolish — it shows a failure to grasp the seriousness of disobeying God. The righteous do not mock sin because they understand its cost. Among the righteous there is genuine favour — God's goodwill and blessing.
verses.prayer: God, help me take sin seriously, not lightly.
verses.discussion_question: Why is laughing at wrongdoing a dangerous thing to do?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a proper seriousness about sin without becoming fearful or joyless — understanding both the weight of disobedience and the grace of God?
verses.do_it_today: If you see others laughing at something wrong today, do not join in. Choose to walk away or speak up kindly.
verses.illustration_prompt: A group of children laughing at a broken rule, one child standing apart with a quiet and serious expression, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The heart knoweth his own bitterness; and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.
verses.little_bible: Your own heart knows your deepest pain. And no one else can fully share your deepest joy.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Your heart knows its own hurt and its own joy.
verses.meaning: There is an irreducible privacy to the inner life. No one else can fully enter our deepest grief or deepest joy. This is a call to compassion — we do not fully know what another person carries — and to trust that God, who does see all, understands us completely.
verses.prayer: God, You know my heart. I trust You.
verses.discussion_question: Has anyone ever tried to cheer you up when they didn't really understand how you felt?
verses.family_discussion: How do we create space in our family for each person's inner life to be respected — their real grief and real joy — without rushing to fix or dismiss it?
verses.do_it_today: Ask someone in your family: 'How are you really feeling today?' Then listen without trying to fix it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting alone with a quiet expression, a soft glowing light around their heart, gentle and tender watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown: but the tabernacle of the upright shall flourish.
verses.little_bible: The home of wicked people will fall and be destroyed. But the home of those who do right will grow and flourish.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wicked homes fall. Righteous homes flourish.
verses.meaning: This proverb contrasts permanence and collapse. The wicked may build something impressive, but it will be overthrown. Even the tent — the more temporary dwelling — of the upright will flourish. Righteousness is the only foundation that lasts.
verses.prayer: God, let righteousness fill our home.
verses.discussion_question: What makes a home strong and lasting, not just a building?
verses.family_discussion: What are we building our family life on? Do our daily rhythms, values, and patterns reflect righteousness that will stand — or something that will eventually collapse?
verses.do_it_today: Ask a parent: what is one thing we do as a family that makes our home strong?
verses.illustration_prompt: Two homes: a crumbling grand house in shadow and a simple glowing tent on solid ground blooming with flowers, watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.
verses.little_bible: A path can seem completely right to a person. But if it goes against God's way, it leads to death in the end.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some paths feel right but lead to death.
verses.meaning: This is one of Proverbs' most sobering warnings. Human feelings and logic can be wrong. A path that feels right — that seems completely reasonable — can lead to destruction. This is why God's Word, not our feelings, must be the guide for our lives.
verses.prayer: God, show me the true and right path.
verses.discussion_question: Why can't we always trust our feelings about what is right?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop the habit of checking their instincts and feelings against God's Word — not dismissing their feelings but not trusting them as the final authority?
verses.do_it_today: Before you make a decision today, stop and ask: what does God say about this? Look it up or ask a parent.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing at a fork in the road: one path looks bright and easy but ends in shadow; the other is narrow but leads to light, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth is heaviness.
verses.little_bible: Sometimes people laugh on the outside while their heart aches on the inside. And happiness that ignores real pain does not last.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Sometimes a laughing face hides a sad heart.
verses.meaning: The outward expression of joy can mask inward grief. This verse warns against assuming all is well because someone laughs. It also speaks to the emptiness of mirth that avoids reality — laughter that ends in heaviness because it never addressed what was truly wrong.
verses.prayer: God, help me see past the smiles of others.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of a time when someone seemed fine but was really hurting inside?
verses.family_discussion: How do we create a family culture where real feelings are safe to share — where people do not need to mask sadness behind laughter because they fear being a burden?
verses.do_it_today: Ask someone today: 'Are you really okay?' and mean it. Give them space to be honest.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a wide smile in a crowd but tears just beneath the surface, soft melancholy light, tender watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man shall be satisfied from himself.
verses.little_bible: A person who turns away from God in their heart will be stuck with the results of their own wrong choices. But a good person is satisfied because they have walked well.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Turning from God fills you with your own bad choices.
verses.meaning: The backslider is not someone who merely struggles — it is someone who turns away in their heart. The consequence is being filled with the fruit of one's own choices — a sobering form of self-inflicted judgement. The righteous person finds inner satisfaction because they have been faithful.
verses.prayer: God, help me never turn from You.
verses.discussion_question: What happens to a person who keeps making their own wrong choices?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that turning away from God — even gradually, in small steps of the heart — has real consequences, and that returning to Him is always possible and welcomed?
verses.do_it_today: Is there any area of your life where you have been drifting from God? Tell Him about it and ask Him to bring you back.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child who has wandered away from a warm light into a darker field, looking back toward the light, watercolour scene with a sense of longing

verses.kjv: The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.
verses.little_bible: A naive person believes every single thing they hear. A wise person thinks carefully before trusting and acting.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not believe every word. Think carefully first.
verses.meaning: Gullibility is not innocence — it is the failure to apply wisdom to what we hear. The prudent person does not refuse all trust, but they look carefully before accepting every claim. Discernment requires active thought, not passive reception.
verses.prayer: God, give me wisdom to think carefully.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it unwise to believe every single thing you hear?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop healthy discernment — able to question what they see and hear online, from friends, and in culture — without becoming cynical or suspicious of everything?
verses.do_it_today: When you hear something today, ask: 'Is this actually true? How do I know?' before accepting it as fact.
verses.illustration_prompt: A naive child accepting everything thrown at them, and a thoughtful child pausing to examine what comes, warm watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil: but the fool rageth, and is confident.
verses.little_bible: A wise person respects God and turns away from evil. A foolish person charges ahead with confidence — into the wrong thing.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise people turn from evil. Fools rush right in.
verses.meaning: The fear of the LORD produces caution — not cowardice, but the wisdom to step back from evil. The fool is marked by reckless confidence: rage and self-assurance that lead straight into harm. True wisdom knows what to avoid.
verses.prayer: God, help me turn away from evil choices.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between being brave and being reckless?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop godly caution — the wisdom to stop and step back from danger — without teaching them to be fearful of doing anything bold or good?
verses.do_it_today: If you are tempted to do something wrong today, stop. Take one step away. That step is wisdom.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child calmly stepping back from a dark edge, another rushing forward blindly with arms wide open, gentle watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: He that is soon angry dealeth foolishly: and a man of wicked devices is hated.
verses.little_bible: A person who gets angry too quickly does foolish things. A person who plans wicked actions is hated by others.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Quick anger leads to foolish actions.
verses.meaning: Quick-tempered people act without wisdom — they react before thinking, and their reactions are almost always harmful. The person who schemes wickedness in a calculated way is just as dangerous — and despised. Both anger unchecked and evil intention produce destruction.
verses.prayer: God, help me slow down before I react.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when you do things in a flash of anger?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop the habit of pausing before reacting in anger — and understand that reacting quickly in anger is almost never the wise choice?
verses.do_it_today: When something frustrates you today, breathe, count to five, then decide how to respond wisely.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with an angry face about to react, then the same child pausing with eyes closed and hands open, warm watercolour before-and-after

verses.kjv: The simple inherit folly: but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
verses.little_bible: Naive people end up with nothing but foolishness as their inheritance. But careful, wise people are crowned with real knowledge.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise people are crowned with real knowledge.
verses.meaning: What you pursue is what you receive. The simple — those who do not seek wisdom — end up inheriting folly as their portion. But the prudent are crowned, as if royalty, with knowledge. Wisdom is a crown worth seeking.
verses.prayer: God, let wisdom be my crown.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to be crowned with knowledge?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children value the pursuit of wisdom as something worth working for — not a default that happens automatically, but a crown they can reach for?
verses.do_it_today: Learn one new true thing today — from the Bible, a book, or a wise person. Treasure it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child wearing a glowing crown made of light and open books, standing tall and joyful, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The evil bow before the good; and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
verses.little_bible: In the end, those who do evil will bow before those who do good. The wicked will come to the gate of the righteous.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: In the end, good wins. Evil must bow.
verses.meaning: This is a promise about the final order of things. Goodness and righteousness will ultimately prevail — those who chose evil will be humbled before those who walked rightly. This echoes the promise that God will vindicate the righteous in the end.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust that good wins.
verses.discussion_question: What does God promise about good and evil in the end?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children trust God's justice when they see wickedness going unpunished in the world — building hope in God's promise without bitterness?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a time when right seemed to lose. Ask God: 'Help me trust Your justice and the end You have promised.'
verses.illustration_prompt: Two figures: one humble and bowing, one standing upright in warmth and light, a picture of the righteous honoured and the wicked humbled, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich hath many friends.
verses.little_bible: Poor people are sometimes rejected even by those closest to them. Rich people gather many friends around them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People often avoid the poor but flock to the rich.
verses.meaning: This is an observation about fallen human nature — not a prescription. People naturally gravitate toward those with power and resources, and desert those who have nothing. God notices this tendency and calls His people to something completely different: love and mercy toward the poor.
verses.prayer: God, help me love those who are left out.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever seen someone left out because they had less than others?
verses.family_discussion: How do we raise children who actively include and befriend those who are overlooked — whose friendship is not shaped by what someone has but by who they are?
verses.do_it_today: Look for someone who seems left out or overlooked today. Speak to them and be kind.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing alone while others gather around a well-dressed child, a compassionate figure walking toward the lonely child, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth: but he that hath mercy on the poor, happy is he.
verses.little_bible: Despising your neighbour — looking down on them — is sin. But showing mercy and kindness to those in need brings true happiness.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Show mercy to the poor and be truly happy.
verses.meaning: The language is direct and should not be softened: despising your neighbour is explicitly called sin. And the person who shows mercy to the poor is called happy — the same word used in the Beatitudes. Compassion is not optional; it is obedience, and it carries blessing.
verses.prayer: God, give me a heart full of mercy.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to despise someone, and why is that sin?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children genuine compassion that leads to action — not just a feeling of pity, but mercy that shows up in real kindness and generosity?
verses.do_it_today: Do one act of mercy today — share something, help someone, or include someone who is usually left out.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sharing food or a coat with a poor child, warmth and joy on both their faces, soft golden watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Do they not err that devise evil? but mercy and truth shall be to them that devise good.
verses.little_bible: Those who plan evil are going the wrong way. But those who plan to do good receive mercy and truth in return.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Plan good. Receive mercy and truth.
verses.meaning: Our intentions and plans matter. Those who scheme evil are fundamentally in error — off the path. Those who plan good receive mercy and faithfulness as their companions. What we plan reveals what we love, and what we love determines where our life goes.
verses.prayer: God, help me plan to do good today.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to plan to do good rather than just accidentally doing it?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children be intentional about goodness — not passive or merely reactive, but actively thinking about how to show love and do right?
verses.do_it_today: Plan one good thing you will do for someone today before the day begins. Then do it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting and thinking with a warm golden glow, sketching a plan for doing something kind, watercolour scene of intentional good

verses.kjv: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.
verses.little_bible: Real work produces real results. But just talking without working leads only to poverty.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Work brings profit. Talk alone brings poverty.
verses.meaning: All honest labour produces some profit — gain, growth, or skill. But all talk with no action leads to poverty. This is not a warning against speaking but against substituting words for work. Words without deeds are ultimately empty.
verses.prayer: God, help me work, not just talk.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between talking about doing something and actually doing it?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children become people who follow through — who match their words with action — and resist the temptation to talk more than they produce?
verses.do_it_today: Pick one thing you have been talking about doing. Start doing it today, even if it is just one small step.
verses.illustration_prompt: One child working with hands in a garden producing fruit; another child sitting and talking while the ground stays bare beside them, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: The crown of the wise is their riches: but the foolishness of fools is folly.
verses.little_bible: Wise people wear their gains like a crown — their riches show their wisdom. But fools only produce more foolishness.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wisdom brings real gain. Foolishness brings more foolishness.
verses.meaning: Wisdom produces fruit that honours the person who walks in it — it is itself a crown. But folly is self-perpetuating: it produces only more folly. The two paths diverge further and further the longer one walks them.
verses.prayer: God, let wisdom be my greatest gain.
verses.discussion_question: How does wisdom produce something that lasts, while foolishness only makes things worse?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see that wisdom is not restrictive but productive — that it actually leads to more, not less, over time?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one way wisdom has already brought something good into your life. Thank God for it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise child with a simple glowing crown, standing in a garden of growing things; a foolish child surrounded by thorns and wilting weeds, watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.
verses.little_bible: An honest witness saves people. A lying witness destroys them with false words.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honest words save people. Lies destroy them.
verses.meaning: Truth in testimony is not just a moral virtue — it has life-or-death consequences. A true witness can literally save a life by telling the truth. A false witness destroys lives. Honesty is never a small thing; it carries the weight of souls.
verses.prayer: God, let my words always be true.
verses.discussion_question: How can telling the truth save someone?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that truthfulness is not just about personal integrity — it has real consequences for the people around them, for good or for harm?
verses.do_it_today: Tell one true thing today that takes courage to say. Let your honesty be a gift to someone.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child speaking truthfully in a group, a warm light coming from their words that reaches and protects another child nearby, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.
verses.little_bible: When you honour and respect God, you gain a real and strong confidence. God becomes a safe refuge for your whole family.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honouring God gives strong confidence and safety.
verses.meaning: The fear of the LORD is the source of confidence — not self-confidence, but God-grounded security. And this blessing extends outward: the children of those who fear God inherit a refuge. Godliness is not only personal; it shelters those who come after us.
verses.prayer: God, be our family's safe refuge always.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean for God to be a place of refuge?
verses.family_discussion: How do our own patterns of trusting and honouring God create a spiritual atmosphere of safety and confidence for our children — even without them fully understanding it yet?
verses.do_it_today: Tell God one thing you are trusting Him with today. Thank Him for being your refuge.
verses.illustration_prompt: A family sheltered under a warm glowing canopy of light, the parents looking upward in trust, the children safe beneath, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.
verses.little_bible: Honouring God is like drinking from a fountain of life. It keeps you away from the traps that lead to death.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honouring God is a fountain of life.
verses.meaning: The fear of the LORD is not just a warning to avoid evil — it is life-giving, like a flowing spring. It actively sustains and protects. The one who walks in reverence of God is kept from the snares of death that lie along every other path.
verses.prayer: God, keep me away from death's traps.
verses.discussion_question: What is a fountain, and why is it a good picture of what honouring God does for you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see the fear of the LORD not as frightening or restricting but as the living, life-giving wellspring that sustains everything good in their life?
verses.do_it_today: Drink a glass of water today and think: God's wisdom is like a fountain that never runs dry. Thank Him for it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child drinking from a glowing fountain in a bright garden, snares and shadows around the edges of the garden kept at bay by the light, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: In the multitude of people is the king's honour: but in the want of people is the destruction of the prince.
verses.little_bible: A king's honour grows when many people are under his care. But a ruler with no one following him is being destroyed.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A leader is honoured by the people they serve well.
verses.meaning: A leader's greatness is measured by the flourishing of those they lead. A ruler with no people is a ruler with no reign — loss of people is loss of honour. This points to the principle that true leadership is about serving others, not accumulating power for oneself.
verses.prayer: God, help leaders truly serve their people.
verses.discussion_question: What makes a leader truly great and honoured?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that true leadership is about serving and caring for others — not about being in charge or having authority over people?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a leader you look up to. What do they do that serves others well? Try to do one of those things today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A king standing before a flourishing crowd of people, then an empty throne in shadow, warm watercolour contrast between honoured and abandoned leadership

verses.kjv: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
verses.little_bible: A person who is slow to get angry shows great understanding. A person who gets angry too fast only lifts folly higher.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Slow to anger means great wisdom.
verses.meaning: Patience is not weakness — it is a sign of deep understanding. The quick-tempered person exalts folly: they give it power and platform. The patient person demonstrates the same character as God, who is described throughout Scripture as slow to anger.
verses.prayer: God, help me be slow to anger.
verses.discussion_question: What is one thing that makes you angry quickly? How can you slow down?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model slow-to-anger responses for our children — especially in the moments when they are watching how we handle frustration, pressure, and conflict?
verses.do_it_today: The next time something irritates you, wait before reacting. Count to ten and ask God for understanding.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with eyes closed and hands open, breathing slowly while a frustrated scene swirls around them, golden calm at their centre, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.
verses.little_bible: A peaceful heart gives life to the whole body. But envy rots you from the inside out.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A peaceful heart brings life. Envy destroys you inside.
verses.meaning: Inner peace and contentment are physically and spiritually life-giving. Envy — wanting what others have and resenting them for it — is corrosive. It does not merely cause emotional harm; it destroys the whole person. The contrast is striking: life versus rottenness.
verses.prayer: God, give me a peaceful, content heart.
verses.discussion_question: How can wanting what others have hurt you on the inside?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop contentment — genuinely grateful for what they have, free from the corroding resentment of comparing themselves to others?
verses.do_it_today: Name three things you have that are gifts from God. Thank Him for each one instead of thinking about what you do not have.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a calm bright heart full of peace, next to another figure whose heart is dark and crumbling like dry bones from envy, tender watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor.
verses.little_bible: Mistreating poor people insults God who made them. Honouring God means showing mercy to those in need.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Mistreating the poor insults God their Maker.
verses.meaning: Every human being bears the image of God. To oppress the poor is therefore not merely social injustice — it is an insult to their Maker. Conversely, showing mercy to the poor is an act of honouring God. How we treat the vulnerable reveals what we actually believe about God.
verses.prayer: God, help me show mercy to the poor.
verses.discussion_question: How does treating a poor person badly insult God who made them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children connect their treatment of vulnerable people directly to their relationship with God — understanding that how we treat others is inseparable from how we honour their Maker?
verses.do_it_today: Find one way to show mercy to someone who has less than you today — give, share, or speak up for them.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child gently helping a poor and ragged child, a warm light from above affirming the act of mercy, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The wicked is driven away in his wickedness: but the righteous hath hope in his death.
verses.little_bible: The wicked are swept away by their own wrongdoing. But the righteous have real hope, even in death.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The righteous have hope even when they die.
verses.meaning: The wicked are undone by their own choices — their wickedness drives them to their end. But the righteous person has hope even at death — because death is not the final word for those who trust God. This verse reaches ahead to the resurrection hope that the New Testament makes explicit.
verses.prayer: God, give me hope that lasts beyond death.
verses.discussion_question: Why does a righteous person have hope even when they die?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a living hope in God's promises — including the resurrection — so that death is not a fearful thing but a doorway into what God has prepared?
verses.do_it_today: Ask a parent: what is the hope that Christians have when someone they love dies? Talk about it together.
verses.illustration_prompt: A righteous figure walking peacefully through a dark valley toward a glowing light ahead, full of calm hope, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Wisdom resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding: but that which is in the midst of fools is made known.
verses.little_bible: Wisdom rests quietly in the heart of the person who truly understands. But a fool's emptiness is easy to see.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: True wisdom rests quietly in the heart.
verses.meaning: Wisdom in the wise person is settled, steady, and quiet — it does not need to announce itself. The fool's inner emptiness, by contrast, cannot be hidden: it comes out and becomes obvious to all. True wisdom has a stillness about it.
verses.prayer: God, let true wisdom rest in my heart.
verses.discussion_question: How can you tell a truly wise person from someone who just talks a lot?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children value quiet, settled wisdom over showy cleverness — learning to recognise that the most truly wise people are often the most calm and unhurried?
verses.do_it_today: Practice being quiet and thoughtful for five minutes today. Let wisdom be still inside you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting peacefully with a glowing heart, full of calm and quiet wisdom, while others rush and shout around them, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people.
verses.little_bible: When a nation does what is right, it rises up and is honoured. But when a people chooses sin, it becomes a disgrace.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteousness lifts a nation. Sin shames it.
verses.meaning: This is one of the great civic proverbs of Scripture. National greatness is not found in military power, wealth, or strategy — it is found in righteousness. Sin, by contrast, is a reproach — a disgrace — to any people, regardless of their strength or achievement. This applies to families, communities, and nations alike.
verses.prayer: God, make our nation righteous and good.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean for a whole nation to be lifted up by righteousness?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that they are part of a larger community and nation — and that their personal choices to walk in righteousness or sin are connected to the health of that larger community?
verses.do_it_today: Pray today for your country, your leaders, and your community — that they would choose righteousness.
verses.illustration_prompt: A bright city on a hill glowing with righteousness and light, beside a crumbling darker city in shadow, wide-angle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The king's favour is toward a wise servant: but his wrath is against him that causeth shame.
verses.little_bible: A king is pleased with a servant who acts wisely. But he is angry at the one who brings disgrace.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise servants win the king's favour.
verses.meaning: Wisdom gains favour from those in authority; shame and disgrace provoke wrath. This principle applies in every area of life — at home, at school, in work, and ultimately before God the King. Wisdom is not just privately beneficial; it shapes our standing before those we serve.
verses.prayer: God, help me serve wisely in all I do.
verses.discussion_question: How does acting wisely affect the people in authority over you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see the connection between their wisdom and their relationships with authority — parents, teachers, and ultimately God — understanding that wisdom builds trust and honour?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one person who has authority over you. Do one wise and helpful thing for them today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A young servant standing before a king, the king smiling with favour, a warm golden light over the scene, watercolour illustration
